note: Energy (MWh) and CO2 (t) per tonne for the energy-intensive refining stages, set beside how concentrated each stage is. Energy figures are approximate literature values; the extremes (magnesium, polysilicon) are web-verified. The point: energy intensity predicts the geography -- the most energy-hungry stages are the most concentrated (on cheap, often dirty, power), and copper (low energy) stays diffuse as the control case.

materials.note: The extreme case: ~78 MWh and ~25 t CO2 per tonne (coal-heated, ~4-5 t coal/t Mg). ~87% China.
~40-70 kWh/kg; sited on cheap Chinese coal/hydro power. The solar chokepoint is an energy chokepoint.
~14 MWh/t of electricity; ~16 t CO2/t on a coal grid (China), ~2 t on hydro. Power IS the cost.
~11 MWh/t; the feedstock for both chips and polysilicon, itself energy-sited.
~9-10 MWh-equiv/t, mostly natural gas; sites on cheap gas rather than one country — energy-sited but diffuse.
~5.5 MWh-equiv/t, mostly coking coal not electricity; ~1.9 t CO2/t. Huge volume, ~52% China.
~3.6 MWh/t; sites on cheap power (South Africa, then Kazakhstan/China) — energy, not the ore.
CONTRAST: low energy intensity (~2.5 MWh/t), so it does NOT concentrate on power — smelting is spread worldwide.
